headline: ASX surged 1.4% today to close above 8,800 as gold hits a record near $4,200 USD — a solid Friday session across most of your holdings.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara had a good session today, closing up nearly 2% to $5.23. Lithium stocks have been getting fresh attention as analysts debate whether the sector is bottoming out — multiple pieces today asking if PLS can lead the next lithium recovery. Still well underwater on your position (-22%), but today's move is a small positive sign.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two jumped nearly 2% last night. The GTA 6 hype machine keeps rolling — reports suggest pre-orders are tracking at historic levels, and crypto exchange Binance even launched leveraged trading products tied to Take-Two stock. The market is pricing in a massive GTA 6 launch.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft had a strong night, up 1.6% to $390.49. No single news catalyst, but the White House announced plans to accelerate AI model standards — which is generally good news for Microsoft given its deep partnership with OpenAI and its AI product suite. The market continues to favour Microsoft's AI story over its peers.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG nudged up 0.57% today to $76.21, riding the broader ASX rally. As a diversified fund with big exposure to global shares, it benefits from both the strong local market and the tailwind of a rising Aussie dollar making your unhedged international holdings worth more.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE edged up slightly today to $95.10. Emerging markets have been a quieter story this week, but a rising AUD/USD (up 0.79% last night) can be a mild headwind for unhedged international ETFs, so flat-to-slightly-up is a reasonable result.

movers.name: Global X Artificial Intelligence ETF
movers.note: GXAI was essentially flat today at $16.74 — barely moved a cent. The AI theme is alive globally, but this ETF hasn't caught fire yet and you're still sitting about 11% underwater on the position. Watch for US AI earnings and product news to be the catalyst here.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: VTS slipped 0.42% today to $533.26 — this one tracks the entire US share market, so it reflects last night's mixed session on Wall Street where the NASDAQ fell 0.8% while the S&P 500 was basically flat. Still up 3.4% overall on your position.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Google dipped slightly last night, down 0.48% to $356.18. No major negative news — analysts are actually asking whether Alphabet will beat earnings estimates again, which suggests the stock is in a holding pattern ahead of its next quarterly report. Google is the one holding where Microsoft's AI momentum is creating a bit of a narrative headwind.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy Companies ETF
movers.note: FUEL was dead flat today at $7.67. Oil prices (WTI crude) slipped slightly to US$68.50 — there's some short-term buying ahead of the US 4th of July holiday, but the broader picture is mixed, with the IEA warning that the Iran conflict is reshaping global oil supply and demand outlooks for 2026.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — Lithium recovery story building
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals is up nearly 2% today and has been featured heavily in analyst coverage asking if lithium stocks are bottoming out. You're still down 22% on your position, but momentum is turning. Worth watching closely this week — if the lithium price starts to recover in China, this could be the start of a meaningful bounce.

watch_today.title: TTWO — GTA 6 hype at full throttle
watch_today.detail: Take-Two closed up nearly 2% last night and is now sitting 11% above your cost base. Pre-order reports describe GTA 6 numbers as 'historic' with no official figures yet. The stock has real momentum but is also priced for a perfect launch. If you've been thinking about trimming profits, keep watching — any delay news would hit hard.

watch_today.title: MSFT — AI tailwind is real, but still underwater
watch_today.detail: Microsoft jumped 1.6% last night and the White House is accelerating AI standards work that plays into Microsoft/OpenAI's favour. You're still 12% in the red on this position, but the direction of travel is positive. No reason to sell — the thesis is intact.

watch_today.title: Gold hits ~$4,192 USD — record territory
watch_today.detail: Gold surged nearly 2% last night to $4,191 USD an ounce — that's exceptional. It reflects genuine uncertainty in global markets (Middle East tensions, US fiscal concerns). You don't hold gold directly, but it's a useful signal: when gold is running this hard, investors are nervous about something bigger. Worth keeping an eye on.

watch_today.title: AUD/USD at 0.6946 — watch the FX impact on US holdings
watch_today.detail: The Aussie dollar rose 0.79% last night to nearly 70 US cents. A stronger AUD means your US holdings (GOOG, MSFT, TTWO) are worth slightly less when converted back to Australian dollars — it's a quiet headwind. Nothing dramatic yet, but if the AUD keeps rising (traders are betting the RBA won't raise rates as much), it'll eat into returns on your US stocks.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — AI ETF still lagging despite hot theme
watch_today.detail: Global X AI ETF is flat today and down 11% overall on your position. The AI news globally is busy (White House pushing model standards, Gemini cutting prices) but this ETF hasn't responded. It may just need a big NASDAQ AI rally to wake up. Hold for now — don't add until there's price confirmation.

markets.summary: The ASX had a cracking Friday — up 1.37% to close at 8,844, one of the stronger sessions in recent weeks. Gold is the standout globally, hitting near-record levels around $4,192 USD overnight, up almost 2%. The NASDAQ slipped 0.8% last night while the S&P 500 was essentially flat — a mixed US session with big tech a bit soft. Oil barely moved at $68.50. The Aussie dollar continued to strengthen, now near 69.5 US cents.

politics.summary: A mixed bag in Canberra today — interest rate warnings persist despite some positive economic signals, a controversial $50 billion datacentre proposal is drawing sharp criticism from Greens Senator Pocock, and the government is moving to regulate cash distribution services. Treasurer Chalmers is also in the headlines for changing conditions on foreign investment approvals.

stories.title: Economist warns rates may not fall as fast as hoped despite positive signs
stories.why_it_matters: Even with some brighter economic data, economists are warning Australians not to expect rapid interest rate cuts. The Reserve Bank has been cautious, and the message here is that mortgage holders and investors shouldn't price in too many rate reductions too quickly. For anyone with debt, don't bank on relief coming fast. For the share market, lower rates generally lift valuations — so a slower cutting cycle could limit upside.

stories.title: Pocock slams $50bn datacentre plan as 'ultimate dirty deal'; creatives warn on AI copyright
stories.why_it_matters: Independent Senator David Pocock has labelled a proposed $50 billion datacentre development the 'ultimate dirty deal', raising concerns about energy use and environmental impact. Separately, Australian creatives — writers, artists, musicians — are sounding alarm bells that the same AI push could see their work used to train AI models without consent or payment. This debate is heating up fast and could shape future Australian AI regulation, which matters for holdings like GXAI.AX.

stories.title: Government introduces bill to regulate cash distribution services
stories.why_it_matters: The federal government has tabled new legislation to regulate how banks and financial institutions distribute physical cash — this is part of a broader push to ensure regional and rural Australians aren't left without cash access as banks continue closing branches. It's a direct response to community pressure and doesn't have a major market impact, but signals the government is watching financial services closely.

stories.title: Chalmers changes the rules for foreign investors — AFR
stories.why_it_matters: Treasurer Jim Chalmers is reportedly shifting the goalposts on how foreign investment approvals work — the AFR suggests conditions are being tightened or changed mid-process, which has frustrated some overseas investors. This could affect foreign capital flowing into Australian assets, particularly infrastructure and property. Not an immediate market mover, but a signal that the investment environment is evolving.

ai.summary: AI regulation is dominating the global conversation today — the White House is pushing to fast-track AI model standards, the UN Secretary-General is urging countries not to delay, and there's a fascinating pricing war developing among the major AI services. Closer to home, a proposed $50bn datacentre is sparking debate about AI's energy footprint.

stories.title: White House pushes to fast-track AI model safety standards
stories.why_it_matters: The Trump White House is accelerating work on national standards for AI models — essentially a framework for what AI systems must do (or not do) to be considered safe and trustworthy. This is a big deal for companies like Google and Microsoft that build and sell AI services, as these standards could shape what they're allowed to ship. It's generally seen as bullish for large incumbents who can absorb compliance costs, and bearish for smaller AI startups.

stories.title: Gemini cuts prices while Claude floods the market with new models
stories.why_it_matters: A head-to-head pricing comparison of 8 major generative AI services (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok and others) found that Google's Gemini is the only one actively cutting prices right now, even as Anthropic launches wave after wave of new Claude models. This is a real competitive tactic — Google is trying to win enterprise customers on price while others compete on features. For GOOG holders, it means Google is investing heavily to grow AI market share, which costs money now but could pay off in usage volume.

stories.title: UN Secretary-General urges countries: don't delay AI regulation
stories.why_it_matters: UN Secretary-General António Guterres made a direct plea to world governments to stop procrastinating on AI rules, warning that the window to get ahead of the technology is closing fast. He's pushing for a global AI governance framework before AI systems become too powerful to regulate effectively. For investors, more regulation means more compliance costs for AI companies but also more legitimacy and trust in the sector — which is ultimately good for established players.

stories.title: China's robotics AI industry warns of bubble risks, wants faster regulation
stories.why_it_matters: China's fast-growing 'embodied AI' industry — robots that use AI to move and interact with the physical world — is itself calling for faster government regulation, warning that too much hype and investment is creating bubble conditions. It's a rare case of an industry asking for more oversight. For investors in AI-themed ETFs like GXAI.AX, this is a reminder that the AI hardware/robotics sub-sector carries speculative risk alongside the genuine opportunity.

sport.summary: Big NRL Round 18 weekend kicking off tonight with Panthers vs Rabbitohs — and plenty of news out of Broncos and Dragons camps. Wimbledon delivered heartbreak for Kyrgios, while De Minaur has a golden draw. AFL coaching drama continues.

stories.title: Kyrgios exits Wimbledon, hints it may be his last
stories.why_it_matters: Nick Kyrgios has been knocked out of Wimbledon and made a sad admission that 'that was my last' — suggesting he may have played his final Wimbledon match. He's also facing a fine after reportedly saying 'I don't care' following the loss. It's a bittersweet moment for Australian tennis — Kyrgios at his best was electric, but injuries and off-court issues have plagued his career.

stories.title: De Minaur gets favourable draw — no excuses now
stories.why_it_matters: Alex de Minaur has landed what analysts are calling a very open draw at Wimbledon 2026 — he's avoided the top seeds in his half of the bracket, giving him a genuine path to a deep run or even a final. Sporting News says there are 'no excuses' now. Australia's best chance at a men's Grand Slam title in years is very much alive.

stories.title: Broncos sweating on superstar duo ahead of Round 18
stories.why_it_matters: Broncos coach Michael Madge has flagged concerns about the availability of two key players ahead of Saturday night's clash with the Sharks at Suncorp Stadium. No names confirmed yet in the available text, but 'superstar duo' uncertainty is a big deal for Brisbane — they'll need to be close to full strength to handle Cronulla. Broncos fans should check the Friday late mail before locking in bets.

stories.title: Gutherson rejects $800k Dragons move — defiant stance
stories.why_it_matters: Parramatta Eels captain Clint Gutherson has reportedly knocked back an $800,000 offer from the St George Illawarra Dragons, creating a significant recruiting headache for the club heading into the second half of the season. Gutherson's refusal leaves the Dragons short on marquee signing options, while the Eels retain their skipper — big news for both clubs in the competition's silly season.

stories.title: Benji Marshall's Tigers turnaround: from written-off to legit contenders
stories.why_it_matters: Fox Sports takes a deep dive into how Benji Marshall has turned the Wests Tigers from a laughing stock into genuine contenders — and argues it exposes a myth in the NRL that you need to spend big to compete. The Tigers face the Dragons on Saturday in what shapes as a crucial mid-season clash for both clubs' finals aspirations. Marshall's coaching rise is one of the better stories in the competition this year.
